gaps.sentence: If I were you, I ___ take the earlier train.
gaps.hint: if I were you plus would
gaps.explanation: 'If I were you' is followed by 'would': would take.

gaps.sentence: That ___ be Sarah at the door — she is in Berlin until Friday.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses logical impossibility: can't be Sarah.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
The report ___ to be submitted by noon tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Has to' expresses obligation with a third-person subject: has to be.

gaps.sentence: The invoices ___ last week, so the delay is entirely our fault.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have + participle' criticises a past omission; passive adds 'been sent'.

gaps.sentence: You ___ use my office while I am on holiday.
You ___ park here — the police tow cars away every morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' expresses a rule you must not break: mustn't park.
